article.summary: Beever Atlas distills team conversations into channel-scoped facts and graph relationships, then serves them through hybrid retrieval, a cited Q&A agent, a maintained wiki, and MCP. The review records source observations only; no runtime or benchmark results were measured.

who_what.text: The project is published under the Beever-AI GitHub organization. The README identifies Beever.ai as the builder and presents Beever Atlas as a self-hostable team knowledge application with backend, bot, web, and MCP surfaces; the reviewed sources do not confirm a maintainer's personal identity.

architecture.text: The root README describes conversation ingestion into a semantic memory store with channel, topic, and atomic-fact tiers, alongside a graph of entities and relationships. The wiki and QA agent consume those stores; dashboard and MCP provide access. It names Weaviate, Neo4j, MongoDB, and Redis as backing stores.

The ADK workflow preprocesses messages, extracts facts and entities in parallel, then runs embedding and deterministic cross-batch validation in parallel before one joined persistence step. AtomicFact includes fact text, score, channel/platform, author/time, source message ID, thread, tags, links/media, validity and supersession fields, and contradiction metadata.

The persistence agent resolves fact attribution from source messages and batch-upserts enriched facts. Weaviate uses replacement-style upserts keyed by fact UUID and records the fact properties needed by retrieval and provenance.

behavior.text: Ingestion batches facts after enrichment. The store exposes UUID-keyed upsert operations; temporal invalidation and supersession fields are represented in the model, and default hybrid search filters out facts with invalid_at set.

Channel fact retrieval uses an embedding and native Weaviate BM25-plus-vector hybrid search, over-fetches up to 3× requested results capped at 30, and applies lightweight MMR reranking. If hybrid retrieval or embedding raises, the capability tries BM25-only search. Results carry message-level source metadata and identifiers.

The MCP ask_channel tool accepts quick, deep, and summarize modes, requires a caller principal, checks channel authorization, returns an answer with citations, and imposes a 90-second timeout. Retrieval tools are read-only.

Channel reset removes synced data while keeping the channel addressable. Full hard purge uses stricter destructive authorization and fans out across graph, Weaviate, QA history, wiki pages/cache, chat history, MongoDB, and media. Per-store errors produce a partial result and are retained for retry.

Read capabilities use principal-aware channel checks against connection ownership and selected-channel state. Single-tenant compatibility mode has broader user/MCP paths; bridge principals do not use that fallback. This records source behavior only, not a measured isolation guarantee.

Atomic facts preserve source message ID, author, timestamp, channel, platform, and optional thread/media/link context. WikiCitation records fact ID, excerpt, permalink, author, channel, and timestamp. The citation registry adds stable source IDs, retrieved-by metadata, answer marker mappings, and permalink resolution.

metrics.evidence: Hybrid semantic/BM25 retrieval, MMR reranking, and cited QA surfaces are source-visible. No answer-quality or abstention fixture was run.
The model stores valid_at, invalid_at, supersedes, and superseded_by; default hybrid retrieval excludes invalidated facts. No correction probes were run.
Reset and hard purge cover multiple stores and expose partial errors; no post-delete probes or external-copy audit was run.
Capabilities and MCP query paths check principal access to channels, with compatibility behavior controlled by deployment mode. No forbidden-scope workload was run.
Fact/wiki source metadata and typed citation envelopes are present; claim-level support was not adjudicated.
Source shows embedding, Weaviate retrieval, capped candidate expansion, MMR, async ingestion, fallback logs, and registry counters; no latency or delay measurements were made.
Architecture and query caps are source-visible, but no corpus-level storage, token usage, or provider charges were measured.

limits.text: This bounded review inspected the root README, package map, and selected current ingestion, fact store, retrieval, authorization, channel deletion, and citation code. It did not inspect every platform adapter, wiki-generation path, or deployment configuration.

Source inspection cannot establish retrieval quality, correction behavior on a realistic corpus, isolation under every configured tenancy mode, complete removal of external-provider copies or platform originals, latency, token use, cost, or storage efficiency. The purge service itself records per-store failures and partial outcomes.
README statements about low latency, cheaper inference, and answer quality are product claims. This review contains no runtime observations, adjudicated quality results, or measurements.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No Beever Atlas runtime, benchmark workload, or tests were run for this review.
The project metric definitions and fixture specify a comparison protocol and synthetic cases. They are not Beever Atlas scores or measured outcomes.
